source.text: Talia dicenti crudelis diva severos advertit vultus, inamoenum forte sedebat Coeyton iuxta, resolutaque vertice crines lambere sulpureas permiserat anguibus undas, ilicet igne Iovis lapsisque citatior astris tristibus exsiluit ripis: discedit inane vulgus et occursus dominae pavet; illa per umbras et caligantes animarum examine campos Taenariae limen petit irremeabile portae, sensit adesse Dies, piceo Nox obvia nimbo lucentes turbavit equos; procul arduus Atlas horruit et dubia caelum cervice remisit, arripit extemplo M alea e de valle resurgens notum iter ad Thebas: neque enim velocior ullas itque reditque vias cognatave Tartara mavult, centum illi stantes umbrabant ora cerastae, turba minax diri capitis; sedet intus abaetis ferrea lux oculis, qualis per nubila Phoebes Atracia rubet arte labor; suffusa veneno tenditur ac sanie gliscit cutis; igneus atro ore vapor, quo longa sitis morbique famesque et populis mors una venit; riget horrida tergo palla, et caerulei redeunt in pectora nodi:
source.text_original: ' / Talia dicenti crudelis diva severos / advertit vultus, inamoenum forte sedebat / Coeyton iuxta, resolutaque vertice crines / lambere sulpureas permiserat anguibus undas, / ilicet igne Iovis lapsisque citatior astris / tristibus exsiluit ripis: discedit inane / vulgus et occursus dominae pavet; illa per umbras / et caligantes animarum examine campos / Taenariae limen petit irremeabile portae, / sensit adesse Dies, piceo Nox obvia nimbo / lucentes turbavit equos; procul arduus Atlas / horruit et dubia caelum cervice remisit, / arripit extemplo M alea e de valle resurgens / notum iter ad Thebas: neque enim velocior ullas / itque reditque vias cognatave Tartara mavult, / centum illi stantes umbrabant ora cerastae, / turba minax diri capitis; sedet intus abaetis / ferrea lux oculis, qualis per nubila Phoebes / Atracia rubet arte labor; suffusa veneno / tenditur ac sanie gliscit cutis; igneus atro / ore vapor, quo longa sitis morbique famesque / et populis mors una venit; riget horrida tergo / palla, et caerulei redeunt in pectora nodi: /
source.text_english: As she spoke such things, the cruel goddess turned her stern face; by chance Coeyton was sitting nearby, unpleasant to the eye, and, her hair loosened from her head, she had allowed the snakes to lick the sulfurous waves of it. At once, swifter than the fire of Jupiter and the falling stars, she sprang from the sad banks: the empty crowd withdraws, and it fears the approach of its mistress. She, through the shadows and the fields darkened by the muster of souls, seeks the threshold of the Taenarian gate, never to return; she knew that Day was near, and Night, meeting her with a pitch-black cloud, confused the shining horses. Far away, lofty Atlas shuddered and with hesitant neck lowered the sky; then she at once seizes the known road to Thebes, rising from the valley of M alea. For she neither goes and comes by any swifter roads nor prefers the kin of Tartarus: a hundred cerastae stood shading her face, a threatening crowd around her dire head. Within, a stony brightness sits in her eyes, as when Phoebe reddens through the clouds by the art of Thracian labor; the skin, soaked with venom, is stretched tight and swells with corruption; from her black mouth there pours a fiery vapor, by which comes lasting thirst and the hunger of disease and famine, and one death for peoples; on her back the dreadful cloak stands stiff, and the blue knots return to her breast.

reuse.text_english: On the other side Pholoe, and Rhoetus mad with much Bacchus, and Atrax because of the maiden’s sudden fight.
